title: Status decision briefing lane
content:
Purpose: Short, customer-facing decision ladder for when inference output quality or latency is degraded. Use as a compact status page update plus an attachable one-page in the post-incident package.

Executive summary:
- What: Transient inference quality regressions observed on a subset of us-west-2 hosts. Automatic fallback routing triggered.
- Impact: Some responses had altered ranking or structure and intermittent extra p99 latency (~200-800 ms) for a 12-minute window.
- State: Traffic routed to fallback path, verification and replay queued, no data exfiltration detected.

Decision ladder (customer options):
1) Observe-only (default): Continue as-is, Redwood verifies outputs and publishes final evidence bundle. Pros: least disruption. Cons: Some outputs may differ from pre-incident responses.

2) Request evidence + replay: For customers needing audit-level assurance. Customer provides sample request IDs and consent; Redwood runs replay and delivers a signed evidence bundle and diff report. Timeline: 24-72 hours depending on volume.

3) Enroll in safe-mode: Pin to verified model class and stricter cache policies to prioritize determinism over minimal latency. Expect 10-25% latency increase. Enable via Console toggle or CS contact.

4) Rollforward (correct delivered outputs): After replay verification, customers may request corrected outputs to be delivered to specified endpoints. Requires explicit consent, legal signoff, and mapping of delivery rules.

5) Pause traffic: Tenant-level throttle at ingress. Recommended only for high-risk flows. Confirm downstream retry/backlog behavior before enabling.

Redwood operator commitments per option: observe-only: consolidate evidence and attach incident ID to traces; evidence+replay: compile request list, run isolated replay cluster, publish diffs; safe-mode: enforce model pinning and adjust autoscaling; rollforward: run approved replay and provide delivery receipts; pause: apply ingress hold and offer bulk replay options post-incident.

Status page short copy (<250 chars):
Headline: "Partial inference quality regressions in us-west; fallback routing active"
Body line: "We detected intermittent output degradation and routed impacted traffic to fallbacks. Verification and replay in progress. No data loss. Contact your CS rep for options."

One-paragraph customer postmortem summary to attach at closure:
"On 2026-09-25 14:12-14:24 UTC we observed a transient quality regression affecting a subset of inference requests routed through us-west-2. Automated routing moved traffic to verified fallbacks but a portion of requests returned altered outputs. We executed an evidence replay and verification pass, identified the root cause (kernel-selection heuristic regression under burst conditions), and rolled a targeted fix. Affected enterprise customers who opted into rollforward received corrected outputs. No customer data exposure was found. Actions: kernel selector guardrails, expanded per-tenant canary windows, and a Console opt-in for replay evidence."

Quick copy snippets for status timeline updates:
- "Investigation started - routing metrics flagged anomalies (INC-4128)"
- "Fallback routing applied to impacted traffic"
- "Evidence bundle generation started; replay queued"
- "Fix deployed to selector heuristic; monitoring"
- "Incident closed; replay results attached"

Customer checklist (tick and return to CS):
- I want Redwood to handle verification only.
- I want an evidence bundle and replay (I will provide sample request IDs).
- Enroll my tenant in safe-mode while verification runs.
- Discuss rollforward of corrected outputs (include contact and legal POC).
- Pause tenant traffic temporarily (specify duration).

Internal open items: finalize consent template with Legal and Finance; decide Console UX for opt-ins; auto-notify top tenants when evidence bundle is available.

Contacts: Incident ID INC-4128; CS contact cs+incidents@redwood.ai; enterprise SLA: response within 60 minutes."
